card.title: Give It Up
card.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me have the medal for the charity auction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only thing I've ever won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it should raise more than the toaster.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I lend it for the display? I still want people to know I won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then present it to the buyer yourself. I'll print your name in the programme; everyone will know whose medal was worth giving up.

mechanism: A tries to obtain B's only medal by replacing ownership with public recognition as the valued benefit.
confusable: Unlike soliciting any donation, A must address why this particular possession matters to B and still seek its surrender.
comparison: D12-a offers named presentation to an auction buyer; D12-b offers a retained case and story while pursuing a signed guitar.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
